cases.C16: “Imprimatur” makes human approval the brand promise: weighty, memorable and apt for regulated buyers. Its ecclesiastical origin adds gravitas, while “Labs” keeps it technological; existing uses are adjacent, not identical.
cases.C30: Provost Labs signals governance by consent, not command—exactly the delegated-authority story CISOs want; academic tone reads as trustworthy, careful, and all domains are free.
cases.C18: Redoubt evokes contained, fortified agents with actions held behind walls until approved—precise architectural fit; Companies House is clear, meaning outweighs niche associations.
cases.C24: Rather than unsettling, the architectural Latin root provides precise, sober authority for gatekeeping; it offers completely clear UK registration, every key domain, and avoids crowded, generic security tropes entirely.
cases.C11: Evoking Roman legal guarantees (*cautio*), it delivers serious enterprise restraint. Clear of UK registrations, it uniquely targets enterprise AI workflows, distinct from India-focused hardware fleet dashcams.
cases.C23: Penstock Labs: sluice-gate precision—capability and information flow only when opened. Companies House clear, exact domains free; no Penstock Labs. Pentera soundalike is minor, category distinct.
cases.C27: Anchorite's chosen enclosure is the point: agents bounded by granted capabilities, not hermits shunning clients. Labs signals enterprise R&D; clear UK registration and usable .co.uk/.ai domains outweigh dormant US LLC.
cases.C14: Vouchsafe Labs can register full .com; vouchsafe.id is biometric identity, not governed AI. Archaic promise suits CISO trust; pronunciation is clear.
cases.C15: Militaristic? Yes—and that's the point. In defence, countermand is the disciplined word for revoking an order, fitting an architecture where AI holds only granted power. Sober, ownable, all domains free, no collisions.
cases.C31: Vallum.ai is a startup, not a fortress; co-existence with one early-stage rival is recoverable. The Roman frontier metaphor precisely encodes architecture-of-distrust—gates, ramparts, sovereignty—better than any generic shield name.
cases.C12: veto.so targets developers building agents; Veto Labs sells fixed-price consultancy to CFOs/CISOs in regulated UK enterprise. Different buyer, layer, and GTM. .ai/.io/.co.uk are standard for AI infra; the name perfectly embodies the architecture of distrust.
cases.C29: Pronounced SEN-uh-shal; spelling is phonetic. Archaic gravitas cuts through 'Shield/Guard' noise, signaling sober stewardship for regulated sectors. Exact .com secured. The medieval steward metaphor maps precisely to delegated, bounded agent authority.
cases.C25: Strong Magna Carta symbolism signals bounded AI authority, resonating with C‑level risk managers. Unique UK heritage, no tech conflict, and clear domain availability outweigh minor council/charity overlap.
cases.C22: The jurisdiction metaphor perfectly aligns with restricted AI capabilities. The offshore association suggests high-finance precision, while 'Labs' grounds the brand in technical rigor, neutralizing any perceived frivolity.
cases.C17: The steward metaphor is the definitive expression of delegated authority. Its rarity provides a sophisticated, singular identity that avoids AI clichés, turning obscurity into a mark of prestige.
cases.C26: Chary's rarity is its strength: precise, legal, and ownable. Yes, some mishear it as 'charity'—but that single phonetic risk is outweighed by perfect semantic fit, zero brand collision, and memorable distinctiveness among generic AI vendors.
